thresholds.note: These control tone and the escalation signal only. Safety routing is an OR and never depends on a threshold.

is_emergency.instructions: Does the latest message indicate a genuine emergency requiring immediate crisis resources?

criteria.true: Imminent danger to self or others, an active suicide/violence plan, or a medical emergency requiring 911
criteria.false: Distressed, anxious, venting, seeking support, or discussing past events, but not in immediate danger

escalating.instructions: Compared with the earlier messages, is the situation becoming more dangerous?

criteria.true: Later messages show new intent, a plan, means, a timeline, or immediate danger not present earlier
criteria.false: Stable or improving; no new risk signals

crisis_type.instructions: What type of crisis is this?

criteria.suicide_self_harm: Immediate risk of self-harm or suicide (plan, means, intent)
criteria.domestic_violence: Active domestic violence, abuse, or intimate partner violence
criteria.mental_health_crisis: Severe episode (psychosis, mania, unable to care for self)
criteria.substance_overdose: Suspected overdose, acute intoxication danger, or withdrawal emergency
criteria.not_crisis: Emotional distress but no immediate safety risk

urgency_level.instructions: How urgent is the response needed?
criteria: immediate: Seconds to minutes - life in danger right now
urgent: Minutes to hours - safety at risk soon
elevated: Needs professional help today, not life-threatening this moment
routine: Can wait for a scheduled appointment or standard support

header.dev_set_note: Thresholds and the safety prompt were developed using these cases; results are optimistic.

definitions.crisis_label: a case whose label field is 'crisis'
definitions.non_crisis_label: a case whose label field is anything else
definitions.denominators: k/n denominators are the TOTAL labelled counts in the fixtures file, not the number of cases that produced a route. A case that errored without a route therefore counts as a crisis miss and as incorrect -- the conservative direction.
definitions.crisis_recall: crisis-labelled cases whose FINAL route is crisis. A miss here means an emergency was routed below crisis: the failure that matters.
definitions.emergencies_below_crisis: crisis-labelled cases whose FINAL route is not crisis (check_in, calm, or a case that errored with no route).
definitions.false_escalations: non-crisis-labelled cases whose FINAL route is crisis. Each one sends crisis resources to someone who was not labelled as needing them.
definitions.correct_strict: cases whose FINAL route string equals the label string.
definitions.correct_lenient: as crisis_triage.main --test counts agreement: strict, plus a check_in label also accepting a crisis route. Reported as a secondary figure only.
definitions.signals: each row is ONE signal alone, over the whole file, with the same denominators as the final pipeline row. crisis_caught = crisis-labelled cases the signal fires on (k) out of all crisis-labelled cases (n). non_crisis_flagged = non-crisis-labelled cases it fires on (k) out of all non-crisis-labelled cases (n).
definitions.safety_gate_alone: safety_emergency is True. Includes the fail-closed verdict returned when the safety check itself errored (safety_failed).
definitions.band_alone: band_route is crisis -- Decider's high band. Includes the fail-safe fallback that routes to crisis when Decider is unreachable.
definitions.final_pipeline: the final route is crisis -- what the product actually does.
definitions.crisis_caught_only_by_gate: crisis-labelled cases with FINAL route crisis AND band_route not crisis AND escalating below threshold AND safety_emergency True. These are the cases only the Bedrock gate catches; without it they would have been routed below crisis.
definitions.non_crisis_raised_only_by_gate: the mirror: non-crisis cases whose only trigger was the gate.
definitions.n_errored: cases where an unexpected exception escaped the production triage path. route is null for those and they still count in every denominator above.
definitions.n_fail_safe: cases where the PRODUCTION fail-safe fired: Decider unreachable (fallback_reason set) or the safety check failed (fail-closed). Routing to crisis there is by design, not an error, so it is counted separately from n_errored.
definitions.n_state_mismatches: cases where the string sent to Decider differs from the string sent to the safety check. Production builds one string for both; anything but 0 means that guarantee broke. A case with no safety checker records null and is not counted.
definitions.n_build_state_mismatches: cases where the recorded state differs from crisis_triage.policies.questions.build_state(turns, max_turns).
definitions.safety_failed_flag: safety_failed is True when the safety check could not reach Bedrock and returned its fail-closed verdict instead of a real classification.
definitions.latency_ms: per-leg wall latency as reported by the server/client, warm-up excluded.

confusion_label_x_route.note: rows are the intended label, columns are the FINAL route. The 'error' column holds cases whose route is null because the triage path raised.

crisis_caught_only_by_gate.note: clear_emergencies selects the crisis cases whose group is 'clear_emergency'; the other crisis cases are multi-turn ones where the escalation signal or the band can also fire.
